/-!
# Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: Spectrum of Sequence
*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [Men73] Mendès France, Michel. "Les ensembles de Bésineau."
    Séminaire Delange-Pisot-Poitou 15.1 (1973): 1-6.
-/

namespace Bugeaud04

/--
The spectrum of a sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 1}$ of real numbers is the set of
irrational real numbers $\theta \in (0, 1)$ such that the sequence
$(x_n - n\theta)_{n \ge 1}$ is not uniformly distributed modulo one.
-/
def Spectrum (x : ℕ → ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
  {θ | θ ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ Irrational θ ∧
    ¬ IsEquidistributedModuloOne (fun n => x n - n * θ)}

/--
Problem 10.4. Let $\xi$ be a non-zero real number and $\alpha > 1$ be a real
number. The spectrum of the sequence $(\xi \alpha^n)_{n \ge 1}$ is at most
countable. Posed by Mendès France [Men73].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
lemma spectrum_xi_alpha_pow_countable (ξ : ℝ) (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) :
    (Spectrum (fun n => ξ * α ^ n)).Countable := by
  sorry

end Bugeaud04

reformulations.difference: The imported equidistribution predicate counts indices 0,…,N−1 and tests closed intervals, including singletons. Bugeaud’s Definition 1.1 uses indices 1,…,N and half-open test intervals.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Changing the index range replaces one counted term, so normalized counts differ by at most 1/N. Closed and half-open interval criteria are equivalent: uniform distribution forces every singleton to have density zero, and their counting functions differ only by the upper-endpoint singleton count. In /workspace/review/faithfulness.lean, `equidistribution_source_iff` proves the combined equivalence and `spectrum_source_eq` proves equality with the spectrum using the source conventions. Neither proof depends on sorryAx.

reformulations.difference: Compared with Mendès France’s original problem 6*, the theorem uses Bugeaud’s spectrum restricted to irrational representatives in (0,1), rather than the full spectrum in ℝ/ℤ. It matches Bugeaud’s formulation directly.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Represent ℝ/ℤ by [0,1). The full spectrum differs from the irrational spectrum only by rational representatives, a countable set. Thus either spectrum is countable exactly when the other is. `Review.spectrum_countable_iff_full` proves this equivalence for the canonical representatives in /workspace/review/faithfulness.lean, without sorryAx.
